validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification, ownership, route, spec and status all independently corroborated; keep the note about the project's early (2018) larger-scope proposal for context only
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/wiki, by a deep source ladder. Two Midcoast Energy LLC / ArcLight Capital Partners PRNewswire releases bracket the build: an open-season announcement (Apr. 26, 2019, verified live) states Midcoast is developing 'its CJ Express pipeline expansion project,' and a completion release (Mar. 30, 2021, verified live) states the East Texas subsidiary 'has put its CJ Express Expansion Project ("CJ Express") into service.' Independent trade press corroborates both the proposal and completion stages: Oil & Gas Journal ran the project twice (2018 initial-announcement article and a 2019 open-season article, both verified live), World Pipelines carried the 2019 open-season story (verified live), and Natural Gas Intelligence (Jamison Cocklin, Apr. 1, 2021, verified live) independently reports Midcoast 'brought the CJ Express pipeline expansion into service' and signed a firm transportation deal with Golden Pass LNG for future feed gas. A completely independent, non-trade-press source — the Todd Law Firm's Texas eminent-domain/condemnation guide for landowners (davidtoddlaw.com, verified live) — separately confirms the project underwent real right-of-way acquisition and condemnation proceedings in Panola/Hardin/Tyler/Angelina/Nacogdoches/Rusk/Shelby counties, which is dispositive against a phantom/GEM-only entity: a law firm does not publish landowner guidance for eminent-domain proceedings that do not exist. This is real, built, in-service pipe, not a hallucination or a mislabeled compression retrofit — the sources describe genuine new pipeline plus a 39,000 hp compressor station, not merely upgrades to existing pipe.
CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission line. Every source describes CJ Express as a natural-gas pipeline moving Haynesville Shale production (Carthage/Shelby Trough area) to Gulf Coast demand markets and, eventually, Golden Pass LNG feed gas — consistent with Fuel=Gas and a transmission-scale (36-in, 1,000 MMcf/d) line, not a gathering/process line.
DUPLICATE: checked against the 45-row roster — no other row describes this Carthage(Panola)-to-Silsbee(Hardin) corridor or names 'Clarity' or 'CJ Express.' Not a relabel of any in-scope row. Worth flagging for the record (not an action on P0305): every source describes CJ Express as connecting INTO Midcoast's separate 'Clarity Pipeline' near Silsbee — Clarity itself does not appear anywhere in this 45-row roster or under any obviously-matching name/route, so it may be an untracked adjacent entity; that is a Discovery question, not a duplicate/classification problem for this row, and no action is recommended here.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Midcoast Energy LLC at 100% is confirmed directly and repeatedly — all seven sources name Midcoast Energy, LLC (an ArcLight Capital Partners portfolio company, acquired from Enbridge in Aug. 2018) as sole owner/developer/operator via its East Texas operating subsidiary; no co-owner or JV partner is mentioned anywhere. StartCountry/State/County (Panola->Hardin, Texas, United States) is confirmed exactly by TWO independent sources: davidtoddlaw.com ('commences near Carthage in Panola County, Texas and extending south to Midcoast's Clarity Pipeline in Hardin County, Texas') and the 2019 PRNewswire/World Pipelines releases ('connect Midcoast's existing pipeline assets in San Augustine County ... and ... the Carthage and Shelby Trough area ... to Midcoast's Clarity pipeline near Silsbee, Texas' — Silsbee is the Hardin County seat).
SPEC, checked against >=2 independent sources each: Length 107.00 mi — exact match in both the 2019 PRNewswire release ('up to 107 miles of 36" pipeline') and World Pipelines' independent write-up of the same open season ('107 miles', '36 inches'); tier high. Diameter 36.00 in — same two sources, exact match; tier high. Capacity 1000.00 MMcf/d — PRNewswire ('up to 1.0 Bcfd'), World Pipelines ('up to 1.0 billion ft3/d') and Oil & Gas Journal's 2018 piece ('about 1 bcfd') all agree; tier high. StartYear1=2021 — the Mar. 30, 2021 PRNewswire completion release and the Apr. 1, 2021 NGI article both independently place the in-service date in that window (the 2019 releases had projected 'early 2021,' which the 2021 sources then confirm actually happened); tier high. CAVEAT (informational, not a defect): Oil & Gas Journal's earlier 2018 announcement of the same project described a larger, EARLIER-stage proposal — 150 miles, starting in San Augustine County rather than Panola/Carthage — which davidtoddlaw.com's eminent-domain page also echoes ('up to 150 miles'). The 2019 open-season releases (PRNewswire + World Pipelines, both independent of each other) and the finished project both consistently use the smaller, later figures (107 mi, Carthage/Panola start) that GEM has recorded, so GEM's stored values match the AS-BUILT project, not a stale intermediate proposal; the 150-mi/San Augustine figures reflect an earlier, superseded scope and are not evidence the sheet is wrong.
HARVESTED CITATION POOL: 9 citations harvested from the wiki page; opened/attempted all 9. Read fully: the 2019 PRNewswire open-season release, the 2021 PRNewswire completion release, the NGI article, and davidtoddlaw.com — all substantively used above. Checked but not usable as citations: the PGJ 'Planned Pipelines' PDF (live, but does not name CJ Express — verifier FAIL, an earlier/different planned-pipelines snapshot), the FracTracker national infrastructure map (live, generic map with no per-pipeline naming), and eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (live, a generic EIA data-portal link reused across many rows in this batch, not project-specific). Access failures, not deletions: the harvested midcoastenergy.com press-release URL times out (the wiki's own link has a typo, 'midcpast-energy'; the corrected-spelling URL on the same domain also times out, so the whole domain appears currently unreachable, not merely a bad link) and the ijglobal.com loan article (301/302-redirects to a Greenstreet product/paywall page and no longer serves the original article; url_verifier FAILs it for missing 'CJ Express'). Neither is needed — the seven readable/usable sources already give 2+ independent corroboration on every field. Additional independent trade-press sources located via open-web search beyond the harvested pool (not GEM-derived leads): Oil & Gas Journal ran the project twice (2018 announcement, 2019 open season) and World Pipelines (2019 open season) — both verified live and used above; S&P Global Commodity Insights and Gas Compression Magazine turned up relevant-looking articles but both 403'd (access failures, not cited).

fills.researcher_notes: Midcoast/ArcLight's own Mar. 30, 2021 release states the pipeline was 'put into service' that day; NGI (independent trade press, Apr. 1, 2021) independently reports it 'has brought the CJ Express pipeline expansion into service.' Two independent origins, both dated within days of each other, confirm operating status.

Both releases describe CJ Express as moving natural gas produced in the Haynesville Shale to Gulf Coast demand markets; the 2021 completion release describes a 'natural gas purchase and sales agreement' with Golden Pass LNG. Unambiguously a gas pipeline.

PRNewswire dates the completion release Mar. 30, 2021, stating the pipeline was put into service that day; NGI's Apr. 1, 2021 article independently confirms the in-service event happened in the same window. Matches GEM's StartYear1=2021 exactly. (No exact day/month is staged into StartMonth1 since the two sources differ by two days on the precise date and StartMonth1 is not part of this unit's owed value.)

PRNewswire: 'incremental delivery capacity for up to 1.0 Bcfd from the Carthage area to multiple Gulf Coast markets' = 1000 MMcf/d. World Pipelines independently reports the same project as 'up to 1.0 billion ft3/d'. Oil & Gas Journal's 2018 article gives a third, independent 'about 1 bcfd' figure for the earlier-stage proposal of the same expansion. All three agree with the sheet exactly.

PRNewswire (Midcoast's own open-season release): 'up to 107 miles of 36" pipeline'. World Pipelines, an independent trade publication covering the same open season, separately states '107 miles' / '36 inches'. Exact match, two independent origins. Caveat noted in the main validity entry: an earlier (2018) version of the project was announced at 150 miles from a San Augustine County start, and davidtoddlaw.com's eminent-domain page still echoes that larger figure -- but the finalized 2019 open-season scope and the completed 2021 build both consistently use 107 mi from Panola/Carthage, matching the sheet, so this is scope evolution rather than a live conflict on the built pipeline.
Same two independent sources as Length: PRNewswire '36" pipeline', World Pipelines '36-in. OD'. Exact match.

davidtoddlaw.com (an independent Texas eminent-domain law firm, not affiliated with Midcoast) states the line 'commences near Carthage in Panola County, Texas and extend[s] south to Midcoast's Clarity Pipeline in Hardin County, Texas.' Midcoast's own PRNewswire release independently describes the same route: growing production in 'the Carthage and Shelby Trough area of the Haynesville Shale' connecting 'to Midcoast's Clarity pipeline near Silsbee, Texas' (Silsbee is the Hardin County seat). Two independent sources agree on both endpoint counties exactly.

Every source (PRNewswire x2, NGI, OGJ x2, World Pipelines, davidtoddlaw.com) uniformly names Midcoast Energy, LLC (through its East Texas operating subsidiary, an ArcLight Capital Partners portfolio company) as sole developer/owner/operator; no co-owner or JV partner is mentioned anywhere. 100% Owner1 confirmed at high tier via company disclosure (PRNewswire) plus independent trade press (OGJ).

summary: P0305 CJ Express Pipeline: existence, classification, ownership, route (Panola->Hardin County, TX) and every spec field (107 mi / 36 in / 1,000 MMcf/d / operating since 2021) independently corroborated at high tier by 6 sources (2 Midcoast/ArcLight PRNewswire releases, NGI, Oil & Gas Journal x2, World Pipelines, davidtoddlaw.com); 8 REFS_ADDED, 0 UNRESOLVED, no existence/duplicate/classification concerns. One informational caveat only: an earlier (2018) 150-mile/San Augustine County proposal was superseded by the smaller, later 107-mile/Panola County scope that GEM correctly records as built.
